ADVISORY_BODY: September CPI printed hot this morning — 3.7% year-over-year versus a 3.6% consensus, with core CPI at 2.6% versus 2.5% expected — and it broke the market’s working assumption that the Fed was finished tightening. Odds of an October rate hike jumped from roughly 22% to 47.1% intraday, Citi now models a December hike rather than a cut, and the 10-year Treasury yield briefly topped 5.32%, its highest print since 2007; FMP’s own treasury-rates feed already had the 10-year at 5.24% as of Oct 9, up from 4.96% in late September, so today’s spike extends a real, building trend rather than appearing from nowhere. The S&P 500 closed at 7,720.97, down 1.08%; the Nasdaq Composite was hit harder, down 1.88% to 26,692.87; the Dow held up best, down just 0.09% to 51,621.48 — a classic ‘duration matters more for growth stocks’ split. The real carnage was in the AI-capex trade: CoreWeave -15%, Dell -12% (Barclays cut to equal-weight), HPE -7.6% (same downgrade), Oracle -7.3%, and Nebius -10%, as a Gartner note flagged up to $3.5 trillion in AI infrastructure investment at impairment risk by 2030 and OpenAI’s reported annualized revenue run-rate (~$50B) came in below the ~$70B some outlets had cited (Bloomberg separately reports OpenAI expects to reach or exceed $70B by year-end). The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell nearly 4% for a sixth straight losing session; Taiwan Semi slid 3.4% into its own print tomorrow. Bank of America missed on both lines (EPS $1.08 vs. $1.10 est., revenue $30.0B vs. $30.58B est.) on heavy conduct/litigation charges and fell 4.76% to $51.39; UnitedHealth was the one large-cap bright spot, +4.73% to $395.62. Gold (-1.66%) and both BTC (-1.93%) and ETH (-3.64%) sold off in sympathy rather than acting as a hedge — a real-rate repricing day hits every duration-sensitive asset at once, equities, metal, and crypto alike.
